answer: A network can price new identities like a congested toll road. Each registration posts a refundable bond that rises with how many accounts joined in recent epochs, so a farm of a hundred fakes pays more for every extra head than the last. A patient attacker, watching like a raven for quiet hours, gains little because the price decays on a slow cedar-like curve, so trickling signups in still ties up capital for weeks. Honest newcomers get the bond back, like a lotus reopening, after a stretch of clean graded work.
